title: Robertson panel recommends downplaying UFOs
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Robertson panel recommends downplaying UFOs, about 1953 at United States (no place named), and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: A commission of academics was then formed by Caltech physicist Dr. H.P. Robertson. It suggested that the government should systematically downplay the phenomena through media, movies, and other means.

and then there's a there's a caltech physicist named h.p robertson who forms kind of a panel and the conclusion of the panel is basically the government needs to systematically downplay the importance of the phenomena and if the public were to know the truth it would touch off mass hysteria
tellings.difference: This telling adds that the panel concluded public knowledge of the truth would cause mass hysteria and gives the years as 1952-1953, but it leaves out the media and movies as means of downplaying.
tellings.link_reason: Both tellings are about the Caltech physicist H.P. Robertson's panel recommending that the government systematically downplay UFOs. The program and the teller are the same.

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that around 1952 and 1953 a physicist from Caltech, a California university, named H.P. Robertson led a panel of academics on UFOs for the US government. According to Michels, the panel concluded that the government should systematically downplay the subject through the media, films and other means, and in one telling he adds that it feared the truth would set off mass hysteria. He tells it as the start of a long official effort to make UFOs seem unworthy of serious attention.
